Title: Delete Texture
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary texture images as needed. Location Main Menu Materials Texture Edit Texture 2D Toolbar Edit Texture Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Texture Edit Texture 2D Toolbar Edit Texture Right-click on the texture to delete. Click Delete Texture from the pop-up menu. The selected texture image is now being deleted.

Title: Edit Button Style
Content: List of Contents Edit Button Style Edit Properties Open/Save Button Style Edit Button Style - Edit properties for the button style. - Select a button style from the Object Browser Button Tab and view the selected buttons properties in the Property Editor. Edit Properties Button Name - Rename the selected button style. Shape - Rename the selected button style. - Click the drop-down arrow next to the Shape menu to view all default button shapes. - Select the desired button shape. - The shape is applied to the button. Width - Set the width of the button style. - The widths unit follows the unit configured by the user in the settings. - To use Ligne (L) as the width unit, please navigate to Main Menu Settings User Settings Others Unit and toggle on the Use Ligne (L) for Button Width option. Thickness - Set the thickness of the button style. Weight - Set the weight of the button style in grams. Open/Save Button Style Open - Click the Open button on the top of the Property Editor to load previously saved button style. Save - Click the Save button on the top of the Property Editor to save the configured button style.

Title: Register Custom Buttonholes
Content: List of Contents Register Buttonhole Add Buttonhole Register Buttonhole - Use custom images as buttonholes. - Navigate to the Main Menu and select Materials Button Register Buttonhole. - Or, select a desired buttonhole style from the Object Browser Buttonhole Tab. Then, navigate to the Property Editor to find the Register Buttonhole button next to the Shape toggle down menu. Add Buttonhole - Select the Register Buttonhole button by following the path above. - The Register Buttonhole window appears. - Name the buttonhole. - Select the + button next to the Image menu to upload a buttonhole image. - Select OK to complete the registration. - The registered buttonhole shows in the following path: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Buttonhole (Select a Style) Property Editor Shape. - The registered buttonhole is automatically saved to CLO-ENTERPRISE Assets_ver. x. x. xx Preferences Button_Preset.

Title: Scale OBJ Trims
Content: List of Contents Transform OBJ Trims Scale OBJ Dimension Transform OBJ Trims - Transform OBJ files loaded as trim as needed. - Select the imported OBJ file loaded as trim and select the Scale button hovering over the trim. - Select the OBJ file loaded as trim and navigate to the Property Editor. Scale OBJ Dimension Via the Scale Gizmo - Load an OBJ file as a trim. - Click on the OBJ and select the Scale button on the right top corner. - The Scale Gizmo is formed with three axes and one square. - Select the Scale button again to complete the transformation. Axis - Click and drag the x-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its x-axis. - Click and drag the y-axis to transform the OBJ trim along its y-axis. - Click and drag the z-axis to transform the OBJ along its z-axis. Square - Click and drag the square to transform the OBJ, maintaining its x,y,z dimensional ratio. Via the Property Editor - Select the OBJ trim to be scaled. - The selected OBJs properties appear in the Property Editor. - Find and adjust properties under the Scale (Local) menu as needed. Scale (Local) - X Type in the value to transform the OBJ trim along its x-axis. - Y Type in the value to transform the OBJ trim along its y-axis. - Z Type in the value to transform the OBJ along its z-axis. - Lock Aspect Ratio: Transform the OBJ file while maintaining its dimensional ratio.

Title: Reset View of 3D/2D Window to Grid Center
Content: List of Contents Zoom Extents All With Patterns Without Patterns Zoom Extents All - Maintain the current view and see all Patterns in the 2D or 3D window. - Right click on the 3D window and select Zoom Extents All from the pop-up menu. - Right click on the 2D window and select Zoom Extents All from the pop-up menu. With Patterns 3D Window - To see all Patterns in the 3D window, maintaining the current 3D view, right click on the 3D window to access the pop-up menu. - When the pop-up menu appears, select Zoom Extents All. The 3D window is adjusted automatically to show all Patterns maintaining the current view. 2D Window - To see all Patterns in the 2D window, right click on the 2D window to access the pop-up menu. - When the pop-up menu appears, select Zoom Extents All. The 2D window is adjusted automatically to show all Patterns maintaining the current view. Without Patterns 3D Window - Right click on the 3D window to open the pop-up menu. - When the pop-up menu appears, select Zoom Extents All. The 3D window adjusts automatically to the center of the 3D grid. 2D Windows - Right click on the 2D window to open the pop-up menu. - When the pop-up menu appears, select Zoom Extents All. The 2D window adjusts automatically to the center of the 2D grid.

Title: Show/Hide Seam Allowance
Content: List of Contents Show Seam Allowance Show/Hide Seam Allowance in the 2D window Show/Hide Seam Allowance in the Print Layout Mode Show Seam Allowance - Show or hide Seam Allowances in the 2D window as well as in the Print Layout Mode. - Navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern Create Seam Allowance - Select the Seam Allowance tool from the 2D toolbar. Show/Hide Seam Allowance in the 2D window - Right click on the 2D window. - Select Show Seam Allowance. - Since Seam Allowances are shown in the 2D window by default, they are hidden when the option is selected for the first time. - Select the Show Seam Allowance option again to show them. Show/Hide Seam Allowance in the Print Layout Mode - Right click on the 2D window while in the Print Layout Mode. - Select Show Seam Allowance. - Since Seam Allowances are shown in the 2D window by default, they are hidden when the option is selected for the first time. - Select the Show Seam Allowance option again to show them.

Title: Reset Buttonhole Style Property
Content: Objective Reset buttonhole item properties to default value (ver2.5.0). Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Right-Click Buttonhole Item Pop-Up Menu Reset Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Right-Click Buttonhole Item Pop-Up Menu Reset The buttonhole item properties are now being reset back to default value.

Title: Order of Use of the Modular Configurator Window
Content: Follow the order of use of the Modualr Configurator window in order to construct and use an user data. To create a configuration file for the Modular Configurator, please follow the steps below: Open the Modular Configurator window Add an User folder by pressing (+) icon Press the Edit icon to switch to the Editor Mode If needed, add groups by pressing Add Group icon Designate the Modular file (.zmdr) to either be displayed or hidden for each group Designate the Modular file (.zblc) to either be displayed or hidden for each group Click Save button to save the structure file in the same folder as the Block Press Exit button when editing is done

Title: General Process of Using Modular Mode
Content: Follow the procedure of the Modular Mode to build and design with your own Pattern database. To build the Pattern database, take following procedures: Open Modular Template Add Patterns or Garments Drag the Patterns into Block Boxes Sew the Patterns and the Block Boxes Save it as a Block file (If there is no Modular file in a folder where the Blocks are being saved, save a Modular file too)

Title: Select a Block in the Modular Configurator Window
Content: Objective Select and combine Blocks as desired in the Modular Configurator window. Location Modular Mode Vertical Menu Tab on the Left Modular Configurator Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode Vertical Menu Tab on the Left Modular Configurator Modular Configurator window appears. Select a desired category from the horizontal tab. Folders appear in order. Select a desired Garment category folder. Modular Structure file is displayed. Select a desired Modular Structure file. All Blocks compatible with the selected Module Structure are now being displayed. Select a desired Block. The Blocks are replaced accordingly. Modify the design as desired and complete the 3D Garment.

Title: Invert Selection
Content: Objective Invert the Pattern selection, selecting the Patterns currently not selected. Location Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (On Pattern) Invert Selection Main Menu Edit Invert Selection Operation Select Patterns that will be deselected. Follow the indicated guideline as below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (On Pattern) Invert Selection Main Menu Edit Invert Selection All Patterns that were selected are deselected, while the remaining patterns are selected.

Title: Edit Measurement
Content: Objective Edit avatar measurements. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Tab Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Tab The list of avatar measurements created on the active Avatar appears. Click on the measurement to see or edit its properties. Name Rename the measurement. Basic Length Check the measurement's basic length. Measurement Type Change the measurement type. Surface Length Check the surface length of the measurement. Measurement Information Check the measurement's information. Show Show or hide the selected measurement.

Title: Adjust Collision Thickness
Content: Objective Simulation thickness is invisible set property that represents the collision limit for Garments to result smooth Simulation. By default, the Simulation thickness from the Garment Pattern is set 1.5mm on each side, for a total of 3mm, and this value is adjustable as required. Lower the thickness value to work on Garments that are more likely to be form-fitting, or increase the thickness value to use as padding and etc. Note: For the same reason, the default value of Avatar thickness (Skin Offset) is set for 3mm. For form-fitting Garments or accurate fitting measurement, it is recommended that Skin Offset is adjusted alongside the Simulation thickness. Location Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window Property Editor Simulation Properties Add'l Thickness-Collision Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window Property Editor Simulation Properties Add'l Thickness-Collision Enter desired rendering thickness value. The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.

Title: Delete All Overlapping Points
Content: Objective Delete overlapping points on patterns/internal shapes (ver2.5.0). When importing *.dxf files created in other CAD programs or cutting Patterns in CLO, two Segment Points can be created very close to each other, below the minimum distance set by CLO. When the aforementioned case happens, the respective Patterns cannot be moved nor edited, but can be resolved by deleting the overlapping points. Location Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) Delete All Overlapping Points Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) Delete All Overlapping Points All overlapping points on Patterns and Internal Shapes are deleted.

Title: Delete
Content: List of Contents Delete Point/Line Delete Pattern Objective Delete points, lines, Internal Shapes, and Patterns. Location Delete Point/Line Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Delete Pattern Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern Operation Delete Point/Line Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern Right click on the item to be deleted and select Delete on the pop-up menu. The selected item is deleted. Delete Pattern Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern Right click on the item to be deleted and select Delete on the pop-up menu. The selected item is deleted.

Title: Fabric Information Preview
Content: Fabric Information Preview - Preview fabric information in the Library Window. - Hover the mouse over the fabric (.zfab) file in the Library Window for about 0.5 second. - The preview of fabric information will appear on the right. - Only fabric (.zfab) files saved in v.3.1.0 or higher versions can see the preview. - To preview fabrics saved in previous versions, save the same fabric (.zfab) files in v.3.1.0 or higher versions. Then, open updated fabric (.zfab) files.

Title: Replace as Pattern Outline
Content: Replace as Pattern Outline - Swap Internal Line and Pattern Outline to replace Internal Line as Pattern Outline. - Select Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to 2D Window. - Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select Internal Line and Pattern Outline to be swapped. - Selected Internal Line and Pattern Outline will be highlighted in yellow. - Right click on the selected lines to access a pop-up menu. - Select Replace as Pattern Outline. - The selected Pattern Outline will be replaced with the selected Internal Line as original Pattern Outline will appear as Baseline.

Title: Pleats Fold
Content: List of Contents Pleats Fold Using Pleats Fold Pleats Fold Options Pleats Fold - Auto assign fold angles based on the direction of the pleats. - Select the Pleats Fold tool from the 2D toolbar. Using Pleats Fold - Select the Pleats Fold tool from the 2D toolbar and navigate to the 2D Window. - Click on the pattern to designate the start point of the pleats direction. Then, drag the mouse towards the direction the pleats will be folded. - Double click to complete the guide line. - Make sure to encompass all internal lines that fold angles should be assigned to. - The Pleats Fold Window will appear. Pleats Fold Options Pleats Type - Select the desired pleats type among following options: knife pleats, box pleats, and accordion pleats. Options REVERSE DIRECTION -Change the fold direction of the pleats FOLD ANGLE - Set fold angle range that will be applied to the pleats pattern. - Choose among Preset or enter the desired value. NUMBER OF INTERNAL LINES PER PLEATS - Decide whether two or three internal lines will be included per pleats. - If internal lines that are supposed to have 180 fold angles are not established within the pleats pattern, select two for NUMBER OF INTERNAL LINES PER PLEATS. - After the adjusting the options, hit OK. - The outside folds will be highlighted in red whereas the inside folds will be highlighted in green. - The pleats pattern will be folded based on the settings when the Simulation is activated.

Title: Transform Point/Segment
Content: List of Contents Transform Point/Segment Rotating Segment Scaling Segment Scaling Segment with Pivot Point Activated Moving Point/Segment Transform Point/Segment - Move, rotate and scale point and segment. - Navigate to the 2D toolbar and hold down the Edit Pattern tool as the Transform Point/Segment tool will appear below. Rotating Segment Rotating Segment - Select the Transform Point/Segment tool from the 2D toolbar. - Click on the segment to be rotated. - The selected segment will be highlighted in yellow as a marquee box appears. - Hover the mouse over the scale point on top of the marquee box. The mouse cursor will appear as a rotating wheel. - Click and drag the scale point towards the desired direction. - The segment will rotate around its center. Rotating Segment with Pivot Point Activated - Select the Transform Point/Segment tool from the 2D toolbar. - Click on the segment to be rotated. - The selected segment will be highlighted in yellow as a marquee box appears. - Double click on the Pivot Point located at the center of the marquee box. - The Pivot Point will be activated as it is highlighted in orange. - Click and drag the activated Pivot Point to where the selected segments rotation should be centered on. - Hover over the scale point on top of the marquee box. The mouse cursor will appear as a rotating wheel. - Click and drag the scale point towards the desired direction. - The selected segment will rotate accordingly centering on the Pivot Point. Scaling Segment Scaling Segment Manually - Select the Transform Point/Segment tool from the 2D toolbar. - Click on the segment to be scaled. - The selected segment will be highlighted in yellow as a marquee box appears. - Click one of the scale points and drag towards the selected segment to be scaled. Scaling Segment with specific value - Select the Transform Point/Segment tool from the 2D toolbar. - Click on the segment to be scaled. - The selected segment will be highlighted in yellow as a marquee box appears. - Click one of the scale points and drag towards the selected segment to be scaled. - As holding down the scale point, right click on the mouse. The Transform pop-up window will appear. - Type in desired PERCENTAGE and DIMENSION, and then hit OK. - The selected segment will be scaled accordingly. Scaling Segment with Pivot Point Activated Scaling Segment Manually - Select the Transform Point/Segment tool from the 2D toolbar. - Click on the segment to be scaled. - The selected segment will be highlighted as a marquee box appears. - Double click on the Pivot Point located at the center of the marquee box. - The Pivot Point will be activated as it is highlighted in orange. - Click and drag the activated Pivot Point to where it will be the center of the transformation. - Click one of the scale points and drag towards the segment to be scaled. - The selected segment will be lengthened or shortened centering on the Pivot Point. Scaling Segment with specific value - Select the Transform Point/Segment tool from the 2D toolbar. - Click on the segment to be scaled. - The selected segment will be highlighted as a marquee box appears. - Double click on the Pivot Point located at the center of the marquee box. - The Pivot Point will be activated as it is highlighted in orange. - Click and drag the activated Pivot Point to where it will be the center of the transformation. - Click one of the scale points and drag towards the segment to be scaled. - As holding down the scale point, right click on the mouse. The Transformation pop-up window will appear. - Type in desired PERCENTAGE and DIMENSION, then hit OK. - The selected segment will be lengthened or shortened centering on the Pivot Point. Moving Point/Segment Moving Point/Segment Manually - Select the Transform Point/Segment tool from the 2D toolbar. - Click and drag the point/segment to be moved. - Move the point/segment to desired place in the 2D Window and release the mouse to complete the movement. Moving Point/Segment with specific value - Select the Transform Point/Segment tool from the 2D toolbar. - Click and drag the point/segment to be moved. - As holding down the point/segment, right click on the mouse. The Moving Distance pop-up window will appear. - Type in desired value and hit OK. - The point/segment will be moved accordingly.

Title: Circumference Garment Measure
Content: List of Contents Circumference Garment Measure Measuring the 3D Garment Checking the Measurement Editing Circumference Garment Measure Circumference Garment Measure - Measure the circumference of the 3D Garment. - Select the Circumference Garment Measure tool from the 3D toolbar. Measuring the 3D Garment - Circumference garment measure can be created on any surface of the 3D Garment. - Select the Circumference Garment Measure tool from the 3D Toolbar. - Navigate to the 3D Window and hover over the 3D Garment. - Yellow-green circle board and the circumference measure will appear at where the mouse is hovering over. - Click on the 3D Garment. Created circumference measure will be highlighted in yellow as its measurement hovering next to the 3D Garment. - When the circumference garment measure is not selected, it will appear as yellow-green line. Checking the Measurement - Check the created circumference garment measure. - Select the Edit Garment Measure tool from the 3D Toolbar. - Click on the circumference garment measure to be selected. - The selected circumference garment measure and the circle board will appear. Editing Circumference Garment Measure - Edit CIRCLE DIAMETER to adjust circle board size. - Select the Edit Garment Measure tool from the 3D Toolbar. - Navigate to the 3D Window and click the circumference garment measure to be edited. - The selected circumference garment measures properties including SURFACE LENGTH and CIRCLE DIAMETER will appear in the Property Editor. - Enter specific value in the CIRCLE DIAMETER to resize the circle board. Be mindful when adjusting the circle board as the 3D garments circumference measurement could not be calculated if the circle board does not fully encompass the 3D Garment.

Title: Tack on Avatar
Content: List of Contents Tack on Avatar Creating Tack on Avatar Tack on Avatar - Use tack to affix a part of the 3D Garment to Avatar. - Select the Tack on Avatar tool from the 3D Toolbar. Creating Tack on Avatar - Select the Tack on Avatar tool from the 3D Toolbar. - Navigate to the 3D Window and hover over the 3D Garment as a black guide point appears. - Click on the desired part of the 3D garment. - The 3D Garment will turn translucent and the Avatar becomes visible. - A dashed black line connected to the first point on the garment will follow along the mouse cursor. - Click on the desired part of the Avatar where the 3D Garment should be affixed to. - The Tack is created and highlighted in yellow.

Title: Tack
Content: List of Contents Tack Creating Tack Tack - Use tack to affix parts of the 3D Garment together. - Select the Tack tool from the 3D Toolbar. Creating Tack - Select the Tack tool from the 3D Toolbar. - Navigate to the 3D Window and hover over the 3D Garment as a purple guide point appears. - Click on the desired part of the 3D Garment. - A dashed purple line connected to the first point on the garment will follow along the mouse cursor. - Click on the desired part of the 3D garment to designate the attaching point. - The Tack is created and highlighted in yellow.

Title: Edit Tack
Content: List of Contents Edit Tack Moving Tack Adjusting Tack Property Deleting Tack Edit Tack - Adjust or delete previously created Tack. - Select the Edit Tack tool from the 3D toolbar. Moving Tack - Tack Can be moved both in the 2D Window and the 3D Window. - The 3D Garment will turn translucent when the Edit Tack tool is selected. - To move the Tack, click and drag the point to be moved. - Release the mouse to complete the adjustment. - In the 2D Window, only the Tack on the 2D Pattern can be moved if were to edit an Avatar Tack. Adjusting Tack Property - Select the Edit Tack tool from the 3D toolbar and select the tack to be edited in either the 2D or the 3D Window. - The selected tacks property will appear in the Property Editor. - Enter the desired value for THREAD LENGTH to adjust the thread length joining the tack. Deleting Tack - Select the Edit Tack tool from the 3D Toolbar and hover over the tack to be deleted. - Right click to access the pop-up menu. - Click DELETE. - Or, select the tack to be deleted and hit Delete key on the keyboard. - The selected tack will be deleted.

Title: Emulator
Content: How to use CLO Fabric Kit 2.0

Title: View Manual and Tutorial Links on Tooltips
Content: Objective Learn how to use tools with manual and tutorial links on tooltips. Location Main Menu Hover the Mouse Over Each Tool's Icon Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Hover the Mouse Over Each Tool's Icon Each tool's manual and tutorial links appear as a tooltip. Click Manual. The manual about the selected tool appears with an internet browser. Click Tutorial. The tutorial about the selected tool appears with an internet browser. Note: Show or hide tooltips in Others setting.

Title: Custom View
Content: List of Contents Create Open/Save Delete Rename Objective Easily open and save custom view of the 3D window at your convenience. Location Main Menu Display Viewpoint Custom View Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) Custom View Operation Create Rotate the 3D Window as desired. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Viewpoint Custom View Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) Custom View The Custom View window appears. Left click on the camera icon on the right top corner. The current view is saved and added to the Custom View window. Double click on the added custom view. The 3D Window rotates automatically to reflect the custom view. Open/Save Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Viewpoint Custom View Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) Custom View The Custom View window appears. Add the desired custom view. Click on the Open or the Save All button. The group of custom views is opened or saved. Delete Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Viewpoint Custom View Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) Custom View The Custom View window appears. Add the desired custom view. Right-click on the custom view to be deleted. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Select Delete. The selected custom view is deleted from the Custom View window. Rename Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Viewpoint Custom View Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) Custom View The Custom View window appears. Add the desired custom view. Right click on the custom view to be deleted. The right click pop-up menu appears. Select Rename. Edit the name as the custom view's name field is activated. Note: Starting from ver4.1.0, Delete All or Overwrite custom views using the right-click pop-up menu.

Title: Colorway Multiview Snapshot
Content: List of Contents Colorway Multiview Snapshot Capturing Colorway Multiview Snapshot Colorway Multiview Snapshot - Capture multiview snapshot of a single garment or an outfit in multiple colorways at one time. - Switch to Colorway Mode. - Navigate to Main Menu FILE Snapshot 3D Window to create and save a Snapshot. Capturing Colorway Multiview Snapshot - Switch to Colorway Mode and navigate to File Snapshot 3D Window. - A file browser will appear. - Assign file name and its saving location. Then, select Save. - Snapshot pop-up window will appear. - Check Save All Colorways under Options category. Select Save. - Multiview snapshot of the 3D Garment in multiple colorways will be saved at the designated location.

Title: Poly Pen
Content: Poly Pen - Draw polygons or curves to request design modifications in the Comment Mode. - Comment Mode Main Menu Poly Pen. - Use the Poly Pen to address changes or garment information. Create Segment To create a segment, click and drag from a start point. Double click to complete the segment. Create Polygon To create a polygon, click on a start point and click to shape a polygon. Double click the start point to complete the polygon. Create Curve After starting a segment, hold down the Ctrl key and click the next point. A curve point is added. Double click to complete the curves.

Title: Freeform Pen
Content: Freeform Pen - Freehand lines in the Comment mode to request design modification. - Comment Mode Main Menu Freeform Pen. - Use the Freeform Pen in the Comment Mode to mark changes or add design detail. - Click and drag on the 3D window while the Freeform Pen is selected to draw lines. - Lines resemble pencil marks are created on the 3D Garment.

Title: Tile
Content: Tile - Repeat recording. - Animation Mode Animation Editor Toolbar Repeat. - Select the Repeat tool to play the recording repeatedly. - The animation plays repeatedly.
